[402 paywall path] pass - fresh user (xss_5c874555@example.com) with users.created_at backdated 5 days in Mongo triggered UpgradeModal on chat send; modal 'UPGRADE REQUIRED / KEEP THE SHOP RUNNING / Your free trial has ended' opened within 1s; no app-code console error (only the browser's built-in 'Failed to load resource: status 402' network log line, expected). No behavioral regression from the DOMPurify change.
critical_code_review_comments: Markdown.jsx inline() runs BEFORE DOMPurify and already HTML-escapes < > & — this means any HTML embedded in model output is first turned into <...> entities (safe as text). DOMPurify then re-parses and only allows [span,code,strong,em,b,i] with class attr. This is defense-in-depth and correct. One subtle side effect: escaped 'onerror' text remains visible as characters inside .ata-cite (e.g. reviewer's [ATA 00 ] renders as literal '[ATA 00 ]' inside the chip). That is inert (no img element, no handler), but shows a raw-looking payload as text. Acceptable given the threat model; consider truncating or additionally scrubbing the payload string inside ata-cite for polish.

Markdown.jsx: <h${level+1}> up to h4 uses dangerouslySetInnerHTML with safe(); a heading line like '# Title' currently becomes <h2> — semantic drift from '#' -> h2 is intentional per code but worth documenting.

ChatPanel.jsx generic catch (line 155-158) still concatenates '**Connection error.** Please retry.' into acc without logging the exception e. Consistent with the reviewer's DOMPurify+logging intent — consider adding console.error(e) here too for symmetry with the 402 catch.
